name: outl_p
synopsis: void outl_p(unsigned int value, unsigned short port);
description: outl_p performs a low-level output of a 32-bit value to the specified I/O port and pauses until the I/O operation completes. It is primarily intended for internal kernel use but can be accessed from user space with proper permissions.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The 32-bit value to be written to the specified port

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The I/O port address to which the value is written

return_value.success: No return value (the function is void)
return_value.failure: May result in a segmentation fault if I/O permissions are not set using ioperm(2) or iopl(2)

bugs: These functions require compilation with optimization flags like -O or -O2, otherwise they will cause unresolved references at link time. They are hardware-specific and the argument order may differ from other implementations.
